long_biography.plain_text:
Investment manager Bill Stewart built his stock-selection process around businesses with dependable earnings growth. He studied management teams closely, used five-year financial models and assigned two analysts to each investment so that research could continue when one was unavailable. His concentrated portfolios typically held fifteen to twenty companies.

Before working in finance, Stewart had intended to become a forest ranger. A temporary exchange-floor job changed his plans, and he attended night school instead of taking up a place at the University of Maine. His interest in land survived: with others, he bought forests and a farm and transferred them to conservation groups for permanent management.
